clue.text: New cold Oscar's caught inducing drowsiness

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so the Oscar letter sits within the word for cold

parts.note: arctic means extremely cold
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fresh chill, plus a cough drug that Oscar takes, leaves someone sleepy.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses and brings on sleep, so the adjective describes a soporific effect.

clue.text: Out of hospital, injured soldiers may be so

indicators.note: taking the hospital letter out of the word for injured removes it

parts.note: harmed means injured
H is the map and signage abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Wounded troops, once discharged from hospital, might be described this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests soldiers leaving a ward hurt; in fact H is simply dropped from HARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers typically carry weapons, so describing them as bearing arms is a natural state for troops.

clue.text: Sailors with Aussie PM in vessel in Welsh port once

indicators.note: in places the sailors and the afternoon inside the container

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel
RN is the Royal Navy
arvo is Australian slang for afternoon, i.e. p.m.

explanation.surface: Naval men travel with the Australian Prime Minister aboard a ship bound for an old Welsh harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aussie PM' looks like a prime minister, but PM is post meridiem: ARVO, Australian slang for afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnarvon is the older English spelling of Caernarfon, a harbour town in north Wales, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Leader of Cubs, about to enter game, disheartened Scouts

indicators.note: the word for about goes into the game plus the shortened Scouts

parts.note: tig is the children's chasing game, also called tag

indicators.note: with its heart, the middle letters, taken away, only the first and last letters of Scouts remain

parts.note: taken with its heart removed
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A Cub pack leader joins in a game while Scouts lose heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cubs' suggests the Scout movement, but the definition is literal: a mother tiger leads her cubs. TIG is a British name for the playground game tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is a female tiger, the mother who heads and guards her young cubs.

clue.text: Official accused on case of egregious adultery at first

indicators.note: the adultery word comes first, ahead of the shell of egregious

parts.note: charged means formally accused
an affair is an adulterous relationship

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: only its outside letters are used

explanation.surface: A public servant is accused in a case involving shocking infidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargé d'affaires is a diplomatic official who heads an embassy in the ambassador's absence.

clue.text: Bad atmosphere, one admitted by grandmother?

indicators.note: the numeral is let in, placed inside the grandmother word

parts.note: grandmother is ma's ma, mother's mother
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Granny's house has a nasty feel, one guest lets slip.
explanation.walkthrough: Grandmother is read as MA'S MA (mother's mother); the question mark flags this playful construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious vapour or unpleasant, oppressive air, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Court's disputatious figure once dropping ecstasy with mere criminal

indicators.note: dropping says the drug letter is removed from the pool of letters
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A former controversial character drops the drug, alongside a mere criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle ONCE and MERE together, then drop one E (ecstasy). John McEnroe was a tennis player famous for arguing with umpires.
explanation.definitionFit: John McEnroe, the tennis champion, was notorious for his on-court tantrums and rows with officials.

clue.text: Area outside of Burundi in mountain range

indicators.note: in puts the edge letters of Burundi inside the mountain abbreviation

parts.note: MT is the abbreviation for mount or mountain

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: only its outer letters are used

explanation.surface: A region on the edge of Burundi lies within an African mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mountain range' reads as one phrase, but range is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means scope or extent, the range over which something has influence.

clue.text: Important order received by troops, as we see it

indicators.note: the order letters are received inside the troops word

parts.note: men are troops, ordinary soldiers
OM is the Order of Merit
to us means in our view, as we see it

explanation.surface: Soldiers receive a crucial command, the significance of which we recognise.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentous describes something of great significance or consequence, a weighty matter.

clue.text: Knock up cocktail of mint and grape juice finally

indicators.note: a cocktail mixes things together, so these letters are mixed up
finally picks the last letter of juice

parts.note: only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: Whip up a drink using mint and grape juice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock up' looks like making a quick drink, but it is slang for making pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock up is informal for getting someone pregnant, which is what impregnate means.

clue.text: Album for storing useless bits of paper

indicators.note: storing means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A photo album used to keep worthless scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumf is British slang for tedious paperwork or junk documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is informal British for unwanted documents, forms and leaflets, i.e. worthless paperwork.

clue.text: Supplier of plugs for computers mindful about date

indicators.note: about means going around, so the aware word surrounds the date letter

parts.note: aware means mindful

explanation.surface: A computer-conscious electrician supplies plugs, careful about the date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugs' suggests electrical fittings; here plugs are advertising puffs, and adware is software that pushes ads.
explanation.definitionFit: Adware is software that displays advertisements, and a plug is an informal word for a promotional mention.

clue.text: Leaving hostelry, Ginny and Jack doing the twist?

indicators.note: the inn letters leave, being taken out of Ginny

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, as is a rating

explanation.surface: Ginny and Jack leave the pub and hit the dance floor for the Twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Twist is a 1960s dance; gyrating is spinning round, a fair definition by example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyrating means rotating or whirling, which is roughly what dancers do when twisting.

clue.text: What might lead to sin over religious work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rearranged letters of a word (such as ins) whose new form spells sin
second meaning: the ..., the 1880s English translation of the Bible

explanation.walkthrough: A revised version of a word could, cryptically, turn it into sin. 'Over' just joins the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Revised Version is a Victorian update of the King James Bible, a sacred scripture translation.

clue.text: America's current engineers receiving £10,000

indicators.note: the engineers abbreviation receives, holds within it, the money letters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
a grand is a thousand pounds, and IO looks like the number 10, so 10 grand

explanation.surface: American engineers get ten thousand pounds for electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests electricity, but it is a flowing river. 'Grand' is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is a major river forming much of the US–Mexico border, a water current.

clue.text: Setters put through tests bound for hard work here

indicators.note: the setters word is put through, i.e. inside, the tests

parts.note: SATS are standardised school tests
the setters of this crossword refer to themselves as we
a hop is a bound, a jump

explanation.surface: Crossword setters subjected to exams face hard labour.
explanation.walkthrough: SATs are national school exams in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a factory where workers toil long hours for low pay in poor conditions.

clue.text: Installers of worktops reported dodgy manufacturers

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, so we want a word that sounds like this phrase

parts.note: people who fit kitchen counters would be counter fitters

explanation.surface: Kitchen fitters were said to be shoddy producers.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterfeiters make fake goods or money, so they are crooked producers of forgeries.

clue.text: Bats sleepily after tail-ender's dismissed in The Oval

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
the tail-ender is the last letter, and dismissing it removes it before the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A cricketer bats drowsily at the Oval after the number eleven is out.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, and 'bats' and 'tail-ender' feed that picture; but an oval is just the shape. Remove Y from SLEEPILY, then rearrange SLEEPIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is a regular oval curve, so the geometric shape matches.

clue.text: French painter heading for salon door, maybe

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so salon gives its initial

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A French artist makes for the gallery entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for' looks like travelling, but it picks the first letter of salon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress means a way in or entrance, and a door is one example, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Skill when pirouetting, and some potential shown by a dancer on screen

indicators.note: a pirouette is a spin, so the skill word turns round

parts.note: art means skill
a volt is a unit of electrical potential

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer's skill, spinning, shows great promise on film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potential' reads as promise, but it is electrical potential, measured in volts. John Travolta danced in Saturday Night Fever and Grease.
explanation.definitionFit: John Travolta is a film actor famous for his dancing roles, especially in Saturday Night Fever.

clue.text: Drop in velocity — could that be right?

parts.note: V is the physics symbol for velocity
is it? is a doubting question asking whether something is true

explanation.surface: Someone questions a reported fall in speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop in' looks like a fall in speed, but it is the phrase meaning to call on.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to pay an informal call on someone, which is a casual social call.

clue.text: Same-sex clothing bank for Jazz Age socialite

indicators.note: clothing means dressing around, so the gay word wraps the bank

parts.note: gay describes same-sex attraction
TSB is a British high-street bank

explanation.surface: A clothes bank for gay people suits a 1920s high-society figure.
explanation.walkthrough: TSB is a British retail bank. Jay Gatsby is the title character of Fitzgerald's The Great Gatsby.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby, the lavish party host in Fitzgerald's novel, embodies the glamorous 1920s high society.

clue.text: Insist on formal address in French language group

definitions.text: Insist on formal address in French
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: forbid the familiar French pronoun for you, leaving only polite vous
second meaning: a large family of related African languages

explanation.walkthrough: French has a familiar TU and a formal vous: to BAN TU is to insist on the formal one, a whimsical reading of the answer split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantu is a large family of related African tongues, including Swahili, Zulu and Xhosa.

clue.text: Taxonomic group excluding European bovids

indicators.note: excluding means the European letter is left out

parts.note: a genus is a rank in biological classification

explanation.surface: A classification of animals that leaves out European cattle species.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus, or wildebeest, are African antelopes belonging to the cattle family Bovidae.

clue.text: Underworld figure, essentially, with huge quantity of acid

parts.note: per se means essentially, in itself
a pH of one indicates a very strong acid concentration

explanation.surface: A gangster, at heart, carries vast amounts of LSD.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld figure' suggests a gangster and 'acid' the drug; in fact she is the queen of Hades, and a pH of 1 is very strongly acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: Persephone is the Greek goddess abducted by Hades, ruling the realm of the dead as his queen.

clue.text: Recipient of the compiler's work, might one say, in tête-à-tête?

definitions.text: Recipient of the compiler's work, might one say
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a made-up word, the one a setter sets for, like employee from employer
second meaning: a tête-à-tête is an S-shaped sofa for two

explanation.walkthrough: 'Might one say' flags the invented sense; a tête-à-tête is both a private chat and a two-seat sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, and the tête-à-tête is a specific two-person couch design.

clue.text: One pushing rock song's intro is getting complaint, but not tons

indicators.note: the intro is the opening, so the first letter of song

parts.note: only its first letter is used

indicators.note: but not tells us to remove the tons letter from the complaint

parts.note: typhus is a disease, a complaint

explanation.surface: A rock musician's song opening is getting grumbles, though not heavy ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music, but it is a boulder: in Greek myth Sisyphus was doomed forever to roll one uphill.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisyphus, in Greek legend, was punished by eternally rolling a boulder up a hill in Hades.
